newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers seek to talk to U.S Army brass in sex trial.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers seek to talk to U.S Army brass in sex trial.

text.p: Attorneys for an Army sergeant accused of rape asked a military court Monday to let them interview Army Secretary Togo West and other top brass about their involvement in a sexual harassment investigation.

Lawyers for Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson said in pre-trial hearings expected to last several days that public comments by West and other Pentagon officals had unduly influenced the investigation into harassment at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground.

Don Hayden, special agent in charge of a sexual misconduct probe, testified at the hearing that he provided daily updates on the probe to Pentagon officials. However, he said on cross-examination such updates were not unusual.
Simpson's trial is scheduled to begin next Monday. He is charged with several counts of misconduct including rape, forcible sodomy, battery, maltreatment, larceny and robbery.

Simpson's attorneys have asked in motions filed with the military court that charges against him be dismissed due to heavy pre-trial publicity, excess influence by higher-ups on the case, and lack of a speedy trial.
They also are seeking -- in addition to the interviews with top military officials -- a change of venue in the case, and credit for the time Simpson has spent in confinement awaiting trial.
Army Trial Judge Paul Johnston indicated he was sceptical of the first motion. "I guess I'm having a problem as to your wanting to try to interview Secretary West," he said.
Army Prosecutor Capt. Theresa Gallagher told the court the requested interviews were unnecessary because there was no further information to be gained beyond the officials' public comments.
Simpson would be the first of 10 soldiers charged of sexual misconduct at the proving ground to go to trial.

Capt. Derrick Robertson, the highest-ranking soldier charged in the investigation, was convicted earlier this month of consensual sex with a female trainee but cleared of a rape charge. Under terms of a plea agreement, Robertson is to serve four months in prison, forfeit pay, and be dismissed from the military.

Staff Sgt. Nathanael Beach, was acquitted in an administrative proceeding of sexual misconduct charges but found guilty of lesser charges including abuse of authority and failure to obey an order. He has appealed.
Two other soldiers charged in the probe received a discharge in lieu of court martial.
Earlier this month, five women who had trained at the proving ground said Army investigators tried to coerce them into wrongly saying they had been raped by investigation targets.
Investigator Hayden told the hearing that the questioning of trainees fell into a "gray area" between consensual sex and rape.

"As the interviews started, it wasn't clearly rape allegations (being discussed), but it wasn't consensual. We were sort of in a gray area," said Hayden, who is in charge of the sexual misconduct probe at the base for the army's Criminal Investigation Division.
